feedback: Iteration 4 (entityR2B, 124.20) is the best result so far, but its slalom line loss was 0.85 per run. The same sensors and controller in iteration 1 (entityR2A, 111.80; mass 0.8, body_length 0.18) had slalom line loss 0.1. The reduced inertia from iteration 4 is therefore the likely cause of the slalom line loss, and the revert is supported. The candidate geometry matches iteration 1, and I state no outcome for it. Iteration 4 also showed that lower inertia helped s-bend progress (0.20 vs 0.14) and oval progress (0.53 vs 0.40), so some of that gain is likely to be lost. Your mass and body_length revert is still the right first test, because line loss is the more controllable failure. Next steps depend on the race. If slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, the inertia cause is confirmed, so try mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18 next to separate the two effects. If line loss is near 0.1 and max_error stays at about 0.063 m, wheel_track 0.10 is the next lever to test, since it raises turn rate per unit of wheel differential.
requested_changes: Keep mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18 with sensor y 0.03 and the 0.06 m span, since this matches the iteration-1 result that had slalom line loss 0.1.
If slalom line loss is still 0.2 or higher, try mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18 to separate the effect of mass from the effect of body_length on inertia.
If line loss is near 0.1 but max_error stays at about 0.063 m, try wheel_track 0.10 to raise turn authority.
